newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Gulf Coast awash in foreign crudes, arb wide.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Gulf Coast awash in foreign crudes, arb wide.

text.p: The U.S. Gulf Coast was awash in foreign crudes on Tuesday, with a few lingering April cargoes still looking for homes, traders said.

The abundance of crudes in part reflects the wide transatlantic arbitrage. The spread between benchmarks West Texas Intermediate/Cushing and North Sea Brent for April was $1.75-85 a barrel, while the May spread was $1.45-55.
Several companies are talking about bringing Brents into the Gulf Coast, though no deals have been confirmed as yet.
Offers are around May WTI minus 90 cents a barrel for late April arrival, while bids are around $1.10, traders said.
Swiss-based trader Glencore was heard to be considering offering its Brents into South Africa instead of the Gulf Coast.
British Petroleum and Koch Oil, which were also heard to be offering Brents into the Gulf Coast, may have sold their cargoes to a trading house, sources said.
Meanwhile, a U.S. company is showing Iraqi Bashrah Light crude for mid-May arrival at May WTI minus $2.40 a barrel.
West African crude remains plentiful in light of tepid European and Asian demand.
Nigerian Bonny Light was assessed at an equivalent of dated Brent plus $1.75 a barrel for early May delivery on the Gulf Coast.
Elsewhere, Ecuador's state oil company Petroecuador and most of its term customers agreed on new Oriente price formulas for most regions.
The new formula to the U.S. Gulf Coast, the U.S. East Coast and the Caribbean is WTI minus $5.60 a barrel, down 80 cents from Petroecuador's original proposal of $4.80 a barrel.
Tosco, whose 18,000 barrels per day (bpd) one-year contract expired in March, decided not to renew its deal as a result of the formula changes.
Colombian Cano Limon for end-April loading was on offer at WTI minus $3.00-25 a barrel.
Other Latin American activity was subdued in the week heading up the Easter holidays.
The NYMEX and IPE are closed on Friday to observe Good Friday. The IPE is also closed Easter Monday, March 31.
